quantity_units: Use the same units as data/factory.json.

scenarios.description: The cotton spinning line M1 unexpectedly stops and requires six hours of maintenance.
expected_operational_impact: Orders assigned to M1 cannot progress while the machine is unavailable.
The recovery engine must account for the six-hour maintenance window.
Other machines must not be treated as substitutes unless process compatibility permits it.

scenarios.description: Available cotton fibre falls below the requirement of the pending spinning order.
expected_operational_impact: The pending cotton spinning order requires 2400 kg of cotton fibre but only 1200 kg is available.
Production requiring the missing cotton fibre cannot be completed from current inventory alone.
The recovery engine must check supplier lead time and procurement quantity before proposing replenishment.

scenarios.description: The primary supplier SUP-01 reports a delivery delay of twelve additional hours.
expected_operational_impact: The primary supplier's effective delivery time increases from 8 hours to 20 hours.
Any recovery plan relying on this delivery must account for the additional twelve hours.
The recovery engine may compare an eligible backup supplier, including its cost and lead time.

scenarios.scenario_name: Combined Spinning Breakdown and Critical Cotton Shortage
scenarios.description: Machine M1 fails at the same time that available cotton fibre drops to a critically low level.
expected_operational_impact: M1 cannot produce during its six-hour maintenance window.
Only 500 kg of cotton fibre is available against the 2400 kg requirement of ORD-1001.
The primary supplier's delivery is delayed by an additional twelve hours.
The recovery engine must evaluate machine availability, material replenishment timing and the order deadline together.
